For a gallon of creek water, use 8 drops of 6% chlorine bleach (unscented, labeled for disinfection) or 6 drops of 8.25% bleach.  

If the water is cloudy, colored, or very cold, double the dose (16 drops for 6%, 12 drops for 8.25%). Stir well and wait 30 minutes. The water should smell slightly of chlorine. If it doesn’t, repeat the dose and wait 15 more minutes.  

⚠️ Important:  
Boiling water is more reliable than bleach. If you can boil the water, do so—boil for at least 1 minute (3 minutes at elevations over 5,000 feet).  
Bleach does not remove chemicals, fuel, salts, or heavy metals. If the creek water came from a road, field, or mine, or if it looks dark or has floating material, it may be unsafe. Use another water source or boil it first.  

(offline reference: survival/water-purification)
